card_summary: Haivision announced information on video wall technology. The company provided details on its products, focusing on low-latency video transport. The use of ST 2110 and JPEG XS compression in Haivision's video wall products enables frame-accurate and low-latency signal transport, maintaining signal integrity over 12G-SDI and IP networks, with support for NMOS and AES67 protocols.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: Haivision's SRT Implementation Reduces Latency in Live Video Transport

Haivision recently announced the implementation of the Secure Reliable Transport (SRT) protocol in their live video transport solutions, aiming to reduce latency and improve signal integrity. This development is particularly significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it affects the workflow step of live signal transport. The SRT protocol is an open-source technology that enables the transport of high-quality, low-latency video over the internet.

Operational ROI

The implementation of SRT in live video transport solutions can save broadcast CTOs significant amounts of money by reducing transmission costs. With SRT, broadcasters can achieve lower latency than traditional satellite or fibre transmission methods, resulting in a more efficient and cost-effective workflow. For example, a broadcaster can reduce their transmission costs by up to 50% by using SRT instead of satellite transmission. This affects the workflow step of signal routing, as SRT enables the transport of multiple signals over a single connection, simplifying the signal routing process and reducing the hardware rack footprint required.

In comparison to the existing approach of using traditional transmission methods, the implementation of SRT in live video transport solutions changes the operational workflow by reducing the complexity and cost of signal transport. With SRT, broadcasters can transport high-quality video signals over the internet, eliminating the need for expensive satellite or fibre transmission. This results in a more streamlined and efficient workflow, allowing broadcasters to focus on producing high-quality content rather than managing complex transmission infrastructure.

Security & Integration

The SRT protocol is designed to provide a secure and reliable method of transporting video signals over the internet, making it an attractive solution for broadcasters who require low-latency and high-quality video transport. In terms of integration, SRT is compatible with a range of broadcast standards and protocols, including SMPTE ST 2110, NDI, and AES67. This makes it easy to incorporate SRT into existing broadcast infrastructures, without requiring significant changes to the workflow or equipment. Additionally, SRT is compliant with relevant cybersecurity standards, such as the NMOS IS-04 standard, which provides a framework for secure and reliable signal transport.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy SRT in a live video transport solution, broadcasters will require a minimum network bandwidth of 1 Gbps and a hardware specification that includes a dedicated SRT encoder and decoder. Additionally, broadcasters will need to ensure that their software dependencies are compatible with the SRT protocol.
  • Compatibility: The SRT protocol is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-20 standard, which provides a framework for the transport of professional media over IP networks. Additionally, SRT is compatible with the NMOS IS-04 standard, which provides a framework for secure and reliable signal transport.
  • What to Watch: Broadcast engineers should track the development of the SRT protocol and its adoption in the industry, as it is likely to become a widely accepted standard for live video transport. Additionally, engineers should be aware of the upcoming updates to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which will provide further guidance on the transport of professional media over IP networks.

The implementation of SRT in live video transport solutions signals a significant shift in the market towards more efficient and cost-effective methods of signal transport. As a result, engineering teams should prioritize the evaluation and deployment of SRT-compatible solutions to ensure they remain competitive in the market and can take advantage of the benefits of low-latency and high-quality video transport.

Analysis: ST 2110 enables efficient video wall processing, allowing multiple IP streams to be synchronized and switched with low latency, supporting high-bitrate video feeds.
